The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. Each round:

3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.

- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.

If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.

You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: deal the hands → the table → prepare the offer → pick a card → last card taken automatically → reveal → record the picks → pass left → hand scoring → pudding scoring → advance → after the third hand.

Actions you may be asked for:
  pick_a_card  answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.system: You are one player in a game on the XColos platform, played by turns. You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. When you are asked to act, reply with exactly one legal answer in the form the question asks for, and keep any reasoning short and before the answer. Do not ask questions back.
records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: deal the hands → the table → prepare the offer → pick a card → last card taken automatically → reveal → record the picks → pass left → hand scoring → pudding scoring → advance → after the third hand.

Actions you may be asked for:
  pick_a_card  answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: deal the hands → the table → prepare the offer → pick a card → last card taken automatically → reveal → record the picks → pass left → hand scoring → pudding scoring → advance → after the third hand.

Actions you may be asked for:
  pick_a_card  answer with one of the options you are given

  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 4, Dirac. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: deal the hands → the table → prepare the offer → pick a card → last card taken automatically → reveal → record the picks → pass left → hand scoring → pudding scoring → advance → after the third hand.

Actions you may be asked for:
  pick_a_card  answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.system: You are one player in a game on the XColos platform, played by turns. You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. When you are asked to act, reply with exactly one legal answer in the form the question asks for, and keep any reasoning short and before the answer. Do not ask questions back.
records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: deal the hands → the table → prepare the offer → pick a card → last card taken automatically → reveal → record the picks → pass left → hand scoring → pudding scoring → advance → after the third hand.

Actions you may be asked for:
  pick_a_card  answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.system: You are one player in a game on the XColos platform, played by turns. You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.

records.system: You are one player in a game on the XColos platform, played by turns. You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. When you are asked to act, reply with exactly one legal answer in the form the question asks for, and keep any reasoning short and before the answer. Do not ask questions back.
records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: deal the hands → the table → prepare the offer → pick a card → last card taken automatically → reveal → record the picks → pass left → hand scoring → pudding scoring → advance → after the third hand.

Actions you may be asked for:
  pick_a_card  answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. [user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: deal the hands → the table → prepare the offer → pick a card → last card taken automatically → reveal → record the picks → pass left → hand scoring → pudding scoring → advance → after the third hand.

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

records.system: You are one player in a game on the XColos platform, played by turns. You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. When you are asked to act, reply with exactly one legal answer in the form the question asks for, and keep any reasoning short and before the answer. Do not ask questions back.
records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: deal the hands → the table → prepare the offer → pick a card → last card taken automatically → reveal → record the picks → pass left → hand scoring → pudding scoring → advance → after the third hand.

Actions you may be asked for:
  pick_a_card  answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Sushi Draft ===

Sushi Draft uses a 104-card deck: 14 Tempura, 14 Sashimi, 14 Dumpling, 6 Maki-1 (1 maki icon), 12 Maki-2 (2 icons), 8 Maki-3 (3 icons), 10 Salmon Nigiri, 5 Squid Nigiri, 5 Egg Nigiri, 10 Pudding and 6 Wasabi. The deck is shuffled once at the start of the game. Everyone starts with score 0 and 0 puddings.

The game has 3 hands. Each hand has 9 picks with 3 players or 8 picks with 4 players, so the game lasts 27 or 24 rounds. One round is one pick. There is no talk.

Each round:
1. Deal (first pick of a hand only): each player is dealt a hand from the top of the deck, 9 cards with 3 players or 8 cards with 4 players. Undealt cards stay hidden and are not reshuffled.
2. Announce: everyone is told every player's face-up cards for this hand, every player's pudding count and score, and how many cards each hand holds. You alone are shown the cards in your own hand.
3. Pick: all players at the same moment secretly choose one card from their own hand. Nobody sees another's choice until all have chosen. If your hand holds one card, that card is taken automatically and you are not asked.
4. Reveal: all chosen cards are revealed at once; each leaves its owner's hand and is placed face up in front of them.
5. Record the chosen card: Tempura adds 1 to your tempura count. Sashimi adds 1 to your sashimi count. Dumpling adds 1 to your dumpling count. Maki adds its icons (1, 2 or 3) to your maki total. Pudding adds 1 to your puddings, which are kept across all hands. Wasabi adds 1 to your unused wasabi. Nigiri is worth 1 (Egg), 2 (Salmon) or 3 (Squid). If you have at least 1 unused wasabi, the nigiri is placed on it: its value is multiplied by 3 (3, 6 or 9) and your unused wasabi drops by 1. If you have no unused wasabi, the nigiri keeps its plain value. Add the nigiri's value to your nigiri points for this hand.
6. Pass: everyone passes their remaining hand to the player on their left (seat 1 to seat 2, and so on; the last seat to seat 1).
7. Hand scoring (last pick of a hand only). Each player adds to their score:
- Tempura: 5 points per complete set of 2 (for example, 3 tempura gives 5).
- Sashimi: 10 points per complete set of 3 (for example, 5 sashimi gives 10).
- Dumplings: 0 for 0, 1 for 1, 3 for 2, 6 for 3, 10 for 4, and 15 for 5 or more.
- Nigiri: all nigiri points for the hand. Unused wasabi scores 0.
- Maki: among players with a maki total of at least 1, those with the highest total split 6 points equally, rounded down. If exactly one player has the highest total, the players with the second-highest total (at least 1) split 3 points equally, rounded down. If two or more players tie for highest, no second-place points are awarded. A player with maki 0 scores no maki points.
Then every hand-only count (tempura, sashimi, dumplings, maki, unused wasabi, nigiri points) and the face-up cards reset. Puddings stay.
8. Pudding scoring (last pick of the third hand only): players with the most puddings split +6 equally, rounded down. Players with the fewest puddings split -6 equally, rounded toward zero (two tied players get -3 each). Players with 0 puddings count for the fewest. If all players have the same number of puddings, nobody scores for pudding.
9. After the last pick of the third hand, the game ends.

The highest score wins. If two or more players tie for the highest score, the one among them with the most puddings wins. Players still tied share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: deal the hands → the table → prepare the offer → pick a card → last card taken automatically → reveal → record the picks → pass left → hand scoring → pudding scoring → advance → after the third hand.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.
